Title: TexTrolls: Identifying Russian Trolls on Twitter from a Textual Perspective
Therefore, in this paper, we propose a text-based approach to detect the online trolls such as those that were discovered during the US 2016 presidential elections. Our approach is mainly based on textual features which uti- lize thematic information, and proﬁling features to identify the accounts from their way of writing tweets. We deduced the thematic information in a unsupervised way and we show that coupling them with the textual features enhanced the performance of the proposed model.

answer:
The paper proposes a text-based approach that mainly uses thematic information and profiling (textual) features to identify troll accounts from their way of writing tweets; the thematic information is deduced in an unsupervised way and coupling it with the textual features enhanced performance [1]. Specifically, the authors model a set of textual features independently for each theme to capture emotional, stance, and other changes in users' tweets [3], using a rich set of textual features to identify IRA trolls [8].

One highlighted textual feature type is Native Language Identification (NLI), which aims to detect IRA trolls by identifying their way of writing English tweets, inspired by earlier work on identifying the native language of essay writers [4]. The NLI features were shown to be very effective at identifying IRA trolls from their writing style [9].

cited_sources.text: Therefore, in this paper, we propose a text-based approach to detect the online trolls such as those that were discovered during the US 2016 presidential elections. Our approach is mainly based on textual features which uti- lize thematic information, and proﬁling features to identify the accounts from their way of writing tweets. We deduced the thematic information in a unsupervised way and we show that coupling them with the textual features enhanced the performance of the proposed model.

Based on our thematic information, we model the users textual features w.r.t. each of these themes. In other words, we model a set of textual features inde- pendently for each of the former themes to capture the emotional, stance, and others changes in the users tweets. 1: (a) Supporting Trump and (b) Attacking Hillary themes words clouds.

Thus, we propose the following features to identify these users using only their tweets text: – Native Language Identiﬁcation (NLI): This feature was inspired by earlier works on identifying native language of essays writers [22]. We aim to detect IRA trolls by identifying their way of writing English tweets. As shown in [31], English tweets generated by non-English speakers have a diﬀerent syntactic pattern .

From Table 1, we can notice that the number of total tweets of the IRA trolls is similar to the one obtained from the regular users. This is due to the fact that IRA trolls were posting a lot of tweets before and during the elections in an attempt to try to make their messages reach the largest possible audience. 4 Textual Representation In order to identify IRA trolls, we use a rich set of textual features.

Our experiments showed that the extracted themes boosted the per- formance of the proposed model when coupled with other surface text features. In addition, we proposed NLI features to identify IRA trolls from their writing style, which showed to be very eﬀective. Finally, for a better understanding we analyzed the IRA accounts from emotional and linguistic perspectives. Through the manually checking of IRA accounts, we noticed that frequently irony was employed.
